final.summary: Recommended: llm-idea:Front-load heavy work into the cool morning. Peak 90th pct core temp 37.95 °C (limit 38.0), tightest margin 0.04 °C, 70% of priority-weighted work done.
reasons: **Gets the most work done, but runs close to the heat limit.** This plan finishes about 70% of the most important work. Even so, the hottest workers are expected to get within a hair of the safe body-temperature limit, so there's almost no room for surprises like a hotter afternoon, a broken fan, or a missed break. Keep a close eye on everyone and stick to the scheduled breaks.

**Kofi and Sam are kept off the hardest jobs in the heat.** Their bodies aren't used to working in this heat yet, so the plan doesn't give them the heaviest tasks during the hottest conditions. Don't swap them onto those jobs, even if it seems faster.

**The other options aren't better overall.** One option gets the same amount of work done but runs workers even hotter, so this plan is the safer of the two. The other option keeps everyone much cooler but gets only about 41% of the important work done. If conditions get worse than expected, switching to that slower, cooler plan is the safe fallback.
Peak 90th pct core temp 37.95 °C (limit 38.0), tightest margin 0.04 °C, 70% of priority-weighted work done.

- Every worker's 90th percentile core temperature must stay below 38.0 °C all shift. Harder work, sun and high WBGT heat people up; 30-min shade rests cool them down.
- Breaks: at most 3 work slots in a row, then a 'rest' slot; at most 2 in a row if any of those slots has WBGT >= 30.0 °C.
- No outdoor tasks during hazards that stop outdoor work. After lightning, outdoor work stays stopped for 30 more minutes.
- Workers who are not acclimatized never do very_heavy tasks when WBGT >= 28.0 °C.
Validity: one entry per slot per worker; off-site workers rest; skills and allowed slots must match.
